$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only one where the verdict's findings array is strictly
shorter than the violation count the same verdict declares, and it pins that this is an ordinary
report rather than an unscoreable one. The CLI parser permits it: assertFindingCountsAgree binds
Critical and High exactly in both directions and bounds Medium and Low in one direction only, because
summarizing a counted Medium in prose is the shape live reports take.
It scored null until scorer v2, when the eval stopped re-parsing the markdown and started reading the
verdict. The old parser refused any report that declared more violations than it attributed to rows,
which refused this shape, so the most common thing a real report does was recorded as a moved
It also holds the pair that keeps recall and score apart. Its hits and misses are misses-two's
exactly, and its score is two points lower, because the ledger deducted for a Medium that no finding
block describes. Recall is computed from the findings; the score is read off the verdict; a change
that started deriving one from the other moves this case and no other.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, from misses-two's report with one more Medium counted.
derivation: The verdict declares 4 Critical, 3 High, 1 Medium and 0 Low, which sums to 8, and carries seven
findings: C1, C3, C4, C5, H1, H3 and H4, each at the line its rule fires on. The eighth violation is
the Medium, which the report counts in its Total Violations line and describes in the naming-notes
prose with no Severity or Row line, so the CLI parser produces no finding for it.
Seven findings, seven plants matched: hits 7, and misses holds L1 (seeded/checkout.spec.ts:19) and
H10 (seeded/orders.service.spec.ts:39), in the order ground truth lists them. All four C rows are
among the seven, so criticalHits is 4 of 4.
Every finding matched a plant, nothing was reported against the clean control, and all seven name a
The counted-but-undocumented Medium is invisible to recall, which is correct. Recall asks which
planted defects the reviewer named at a place a reader can go and look; a violation with no row and no
location names none. It is not invisible to the score, which is where the deduction lands.
The counts the harness derives from these: recall 7/9 = 0.7778, CRITICAL recall 4/4 = 1.00,
The verdict's own numbers come from cli/lib/parse-report.js reading this report:
100 - 4x10 - 3x5 - 1x2 - 0x1 = 43, and any Critical at all forces Block.
No finding names a file outside the review set, so outOfScope is 0 and falsePositives is unchanged by it.
